subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In an enzyme-catalysed reaction, doubling the enzyme concentration while keeping substrate in large excess will:
options: halve the rate
have no effect on the initial rate
cause denaturation
approximately double the initial rate of reaction
questions.explain: With excess substrate, the number of available active sites limits the rate, so doubling enzyme concentration roughly doubles the rate.

questions.q: Adding solute to pure water causes the water potential to:
options: become more positive
remain at zero
double
become more negative
questions.explain: Solute molecules lower the free energy of water, making the solute (and overall) potential more negative than zero.

questions.q: Spongy mesophyll in a leaf is adapted for gas exchange because:
options: It contains many chloroplasts for trapping light
Air spaces between loosely packed cells provide a large moist surface for diffusion
It transports water to the stomata
It actively pumps carbon dioxide into the cells
questions.explain: Loosely packed cells with interconnected air spaces give a large moist surface area, allowing gases to diffuse to and from photosynthesising cells.

questions.q: The water potential of pure water at standard temperature and pressure is:
options: equal to the solute potential of the cell
zero
always negative
a large positive value
questions.explain: Pure water has the highest water potential, defined as 0 kPa; adding solute makes the water potential more negative.

questions.q: The fluid-mosaic model describes the cell membrane as:
options: a single layer of phospholipids
a continuous protein sheet with no lipid
a rigid layer of protein sandwiched between lipid
a fluid phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in a mosaic pattern
questions.explain: The model depicts a fluid bilayer in which proteins are scattered like a mosaic and can move laterally within the membrane.

questions.q: During inspiration in a mammal, the pressure in the thorax falls because:
options: Surfactant reduces the surface tension of the alveoli
The diaphragm relaxes and domes upward
The volume of the thoracic cavity increases as the diaphragm flattens and the ribs move up and out
The external intercostal muscles relax
questions.explain: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure below atmospheric so air flows in.

questions.q: Why can small non-polar molecules such as oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the membrane by simple diffusion?
options: They are repelled by the hydrophobic core
They are small and non-polar, so they dissolve in and pass through the hydrophobic phospholipid bilayer
They are actively transported
They require carrier proteins
questions.explain: Being small and non-polar, these molecules dissolve in the lipid bilayer and diffuse directly across down their gradient.

options: the rate of reaction at zero substrate
the optimum temperature for the enzyme
the maximum rate of reaction when all active sites are saturated with substrate
the substrate concentration at which the enzyme denatures
questions.explain: Vmax is the theoretical maximum rate achieved when enzyme active sites are fully saturated and working at capacity.

questions.q: Which factor would increase the permeability of a cell membrane?
options: A decrease in temperature, increasing phospholipid order
An increase in temperature, increasing phospholipid movement and creating gaps
Increasing cholesterol content
Removal of all membrane proteins
questions.explain: Higher temperatures increase phospholipid kinetic energy and fluidity, and can denature membrane proteins, increasing permeability.

questions.q: Enzymes increase the rate of reaction by:
options: lowering the activation energy by providing an alternative reaction pathway
raising the temperature of the substrate
increasing the activation energy of the reaction
being permanently changed by the reaction
questions.explain: Enzymes lower the activation energy required, allowing more substrate molecules to react at a given temperature.

questions.q: Tissue fluid is formed at the arteriole end of a capillary mainly because:
options: Plasma proteins leave the capillary
The low water potential of the blood draws water out
Hydrostatic (blood) pressure exceeds the oncotic pull of plasma proteins, forcing fluid out
Oncotic pressure exceeds hydrostatic pressure
questions.explain: At the arteriole end high hydrostatic pressure outweighs the water potential gradient created by plasma proteins, so fluid is forced out.

binding to the active site and blocking substrate entry
binding to an allosteric site away from the active site, altering the active site shape
increasing substrate affinity
questions.explain: Non-competitive inhibitors bind at a site other than the active site, changing the enzyme's tertiary structure so substrate can no longer bind effectively.
